newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia urges peaceful end to Sudan conflict.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia urges peaceful end to Sudan conflict.

text.p: Ethiopia said on Tuesday it and Eritrea should seek a peaceful solution to conflict in Sudan despite Khartoum accusing both countries of invading in support of rebel forces.

"Despite provocations and propaganda campaign on the part of the radical Islamist government in Khartoum, Ethiopia and Eritrea should remain vigorous in seeking peaceful and lasting solutions to problems in Sudan," Ethiopian President Negasso Gidada said in the capital.
"Eritrea and Ethiopia must handle cautiously the crisis in the Sudan," he was quoted as saying by the state news agency.
Sudan says Ethiopian troops are fighting alongside Sudanese rebels in the southeast. It says Eritrea is abetting other rebels to the north and expects a third front to open bordering on Uganda.
But the Ethiopian president made no reference in his comments to the departing Eritrean ambassador to Ethiopia about the accusations by Khartoum, which Addis Ababa and Asmara deny.
He said efforts to build peace in the sub-region by Ethiopia and Eritrea had African and other international backing.
Sudan said on Saturday it had repelled invading Ethiopian forces, killing 17 soldiers and wounding several in clashes in the southeast of the country. It did not say when the clash took place.
Ethiopia's relations with Sudan have been chilly since Addis Ababa accused Khartoum of harbouring gunmen who attempted to assassinate Egypt's president in the Ethiopian capital in 1995.
Eritrea broke diplomatic relations with Sudan in December 1994.
